result.title: When Figures Disagree with Text: Evaluating Autonomous Visual Evidence Verification in Scientific Papers
result.summary: Scientific figures carry evidence for the claims that cite them, so reviewing a paper means checking that a figure agrees with the text, and not only describing what the figure shows. Benchmarks of figure-text verification typically hand the model the figure, the claim, or the knowledge that an inconsistency exists, which leaves untested whether a model can find the figure worth checking in a complete paper, relate a visual element to the claim it conflicts with, and recognize the conflict. We study this autonomous setting on 31 full manuscripts, each carrying a reviewer-documented figure-text inconsistency from PRISMM-Bench that is hidden from the model. Six multimodal models review each PDF under a neutral prompt, and we then add one input at a time to the same manuscripts. Of 1,445 open-ended reviews, 60.6% mention the flawed figure, yet a grading rubric accepts only 3.3% as diagnosing its contradiction; a blind audit finds the rubric lenient, so we read these as rubric-accepted rates and compare conditions rather than absolute values. In a separate controlled run, naming the figure, without stating that it is flawed, raises rubric-accepted diagnosis from 4.3% to 20.4%, while a consistency instruction and coarse visual cues do not. When the contradiction is visible only in the rendered figure, text-only review yields no accepted diagnosis, while review of the rendered pages with the figure named reaches 15.8%. A baseline that lets the model choose which figures to check, ranked by centrality, stays at 4.8%. Deciding what to verify is thus a large part of the difficulty, and the selection rule we tested does not resolve it. Multimodal document understanding should be evaluated on whether a model can propose what to verify, not only answer questions about a figure it is handed.

AI.brief_summary: 研究在 31 篇完整论文 PDF 上评测多模态模型能否自主定位值得核查的图、将其与文中论断关联并识别隐藏的图文矛盾；用六种模型做开放式审稿，逐步加入图名、一致性指令与粗视觉线索，并与按中心度选图的基线比较。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接提供视觉证据筛选与自主核查失败的诊断基准，显示「决定核查什么」是主要瓶颈，对 LOOK 阶段的证据获取、停止决策及视觉内容是否真正被使用的评价有明确参考价值；其评分口径与提示条件可供核查。
